Maria: Heads up — canary for svc-inference-eu has a KV cache hit-rate regression for RAG chat workloads after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (fused-attn-v2 turned on).
Maria: Baseline (master before change): prefix_hit=0.78, overall_token_hit=0.64, p95=72ms
Maria: Canary (fused-attn-v2): prefix_hit=0.33, overall_token_hit=0.28, p95=185ms, evict_count=812
Ajay: yikes. do we have flame graphs or a profile?
Maria: dropping a small profiling snippet — inline logs from kvcache: 
```
kvcache.cpp: collect_stats() {
  total_prefixes=12345
  avg_prefix_len=128
  canonicalized_keys=11890
  collisions_detected=410
  evict_count=812
  hit_rate_prefix=0.33
}
```
Maria: also noticed a dramatic increase in unique cache keys for RAG retrieval-driven prompts (many small per-request metadata tokens getting into the key).
Leo: was the kernel change supposed to affect cache behavior? seems like a runtime thing but maybe fused kernels change execution order and flush patterns?
Ajay: fused-attn-v2 changed tokenization alignment + small differences in kv-store eviction timing because we now pre-allocate different block sizes. Not intended to change keying but can trigger different access patterns.
Sarah: could the batching heuristic be amplifying the problem? dynamic batching took more diverse prompt permutations into a single batch so the KV prefixes being cached are more fragmented.
Ajay: yes — we recently adjusted batch coalescing window from 8ms->12ms for throughput. That increases cross-request mixing. If keying is sensitive to whitespace/metadata ordering, you get more cardinality.
Maria: example cache key we saw (sanitized):
```
conv_id=conv_74 user_meta={session=xyz,device=ios,ts=1718674090} prefix="System: summarize, user: ..." -> key_hash=0x9af3b2
conv_id=conv_74 user_meta={device=ios,session=xyz,ts=1718674091} prefix="System: summarize, user: ..." -> key_hash=0x1c2f7a
```
Maria: same semantic prefix but different ts field causing different keys.
Leo: aha. we never canonicalize/remove session-specific fields from the cache key for RAG preprompt. That explains collisions and low hit-rates.
Sarah: quick tests: if we normalize keys by stripping timestamp and ordering JSON fields, simulated workload hit-rate jumps from 0.33 -> 0.71 in our offline replay.
Ajay: great data. two possible interventions: 1) quick patch to canonicalize & normalize keys (low-risk) 2) revert fused-attn-v2 kernel selection on canary (safer rollback) 3) tune batching window back to 8ms and test.
Maria: priority: mitigate customer impact. Suggest do #1 + #2 on canary, then run replay and live smoke. #1 should be rolled quickly to hosted canaries.
Leo: can we do canonicalization as a lightweight transform in the routing layer instead of runtime kvcache? That avoids tight runtime churn.
Ajay: yes that's doable — stringify prefix content with deterministic ordering, normalized whitespace, drop session/ts fields from any embedded metadata. I'll draft a small filter in the request pipeline.
Sarah: for longer term, we should add unit tests for cache-key stability across kernel variants + a gating perf test (hit-rate delta < 5% for core workloads).
Maria: note: regressions worse for RAG chat vs straight completions. Completions hit-rate only dropped 8%, RAG chat dropped 55% — probably because RAG includes per-retrieval metadata blob in the prompt.
Ajay: also observed structured-output prompts (json-schema) produce longer canonicalization paths — need to ensure we don't blow up CPU with heavy normalization. Keep it cheap: regex strip timestamps + stable JSON key sort.
deploy-bot: deployment 2024-06-18T11:07:22Z started: canary/fused-attn-v2 -> nodeset-7
Maria: action items: @Ajay implement filter + smoke tests (ETA 3h), @Leo revert kernel on canary if quick rollback possible (ETA 30m), @Sarah add replay-based hit-rate regression test to CI (ETA EOD). I'll monitor metrics.
Leo: I'll open a quick PR to rollback and patch routing filter after Ajay's stub.
Ajay: starting local replay now, will post results.
Maria: thanks team. keeping this thread for followups — please paste perf numbers here. :thumbsup:
